newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt wins confidence vote on transport bill.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt wins confidence vote on transport bill.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government won a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament on Friday on a bill covering the reorganisation of the transport sector, a parliamentary official said.

It was the second do-or-die confidence vote Prime Minister Romano Prodi has held this week in a bid to meet tight new deadlines for the ratification of cabinet decree laws and overcome opposition filibustering.

The vote in the Chamber of Deputies, where Prodi depends on the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for his majority, was carried by 308 to 170, officials said. If a government loses a confidence motion it must resign.

Prodi's government has resorted to numerous confidence votes during its 10 months in office, following a court decision banning the cabinet from re-issuing decrees, which expire after 60 days unless passed into law by parliament.

Friday's vote was on an umbrella amendment covering unratified articles of the decree, which must be approved by Wednesday. It reforms the fiscal system for the transport sector and cuts the number of motorway tariffs for haulage companies.

The centre-right bloc headed by Silvio Berlusconi has condemned the regular use of confidence votes, which put bills on the legislative fast-track and brush aside opposition amendments, saying it runs against the spirit of democracy.
